src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: Recently Government of India declared ______ as Ayurveda Day.
On which date is the International Day of Charity, observed by the UN since 2012, held?
x: The International Day of Charity is on 5 September, the same day as Teachers' Day in India.

s: Which theme is associated with World Ozone Day in 2026?
o: Global Action for a Cooler Planet
x: The 2026 theme of World Ozone Day is "Global Action for a Cooler Planet." "Safe care for noncommunicable diseases" is the theme of World Patient Safety Day.

s: What was the 2025 theme of the International Day of Sign Languages?
o: No Human Rights Without Sign Language Rights
x: The 2025 theme of the International Day of Sign Languages, observed on 23 September, was “No Human Rights Without Sign Language Rights”.

s: In which year was the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies, set by the UNGA in 2019, first observed?
x: The UNGA set the day in 2019, but it was first observed in 2020, on 7 September.

s: In which year was Hindi in Devanagari adopted, the event marked by Hindi Diwas on 14 September?
x: Hindi Diwas marks the 1949 adoption of Hindi in Devanagari; it has been observed since 1953.

s: Since which year has International Literacy Day (8 September) been observed?
x: International Literacy Day, a UNESCO day, has been observed since 1967.

s:
Assertion (A): National Forest Martyrs Day is observed on September 11.
Reason (R): It honours forest personnel who died on duty.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason explains the significance of National Forest Martyrs Day. The day is associated with forest personnel who died on duty and is observed on September 11.

s: Antyodaya Diwas on 25 September marks the birth anniversary of whom?
x: Antyodaya Diwas (25 September) marks Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya's birth anniversary.

s: What is the 2026 theme of World Tourism Day?
o: Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day
Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism
x: The 2026 theme of World Tourism Day is "Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism." "Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day" is the theme of the International Day of Peace.

s: Under which formula did the Constituent Assembly adopt Hindi as the Union's official language in 1949, the event marked by Hindi Diwas?
x: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14 September and commemorates the 1949 adoption of Hindi under the Munshi-Ayyangar formula.

s: Which ministry fixed Ayurveda Day on 23 September from 2025?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: The change was made by the Union government through the Ministry of Ayush.

s: By what name is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies marked in India?
x: India observes the day as Swachh Vayu Diwas, when the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan awards are given.

s: Why was Ayurveda Day fixed on 23 September from 2025?
x: Ayurveda Day is on the autumnal equinox (23 September); Yoga Day is on the summer solstice (21 June).

s: What was the 2025 theme of Ayurveda Day?
o: Global Action for a Cooler Planet
x: The 2025 theme was 'Ayurveda for People and Planet'; 'Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow' is the 2026 theme.

s: Since which year has Hindi Diwas (14 September) been observed?
x: The Constituent Assembly's decision came in 1949; Hindi Diwas has been observed since 1953.

s: Which of the following pairs (day – person) is correctly matched?
x: Engineer's Day marks Visvesvaraya's birth; Teachers' Day is Radhakrishnan's, Antyodaya Diwas Deendayal Upadhyaya's and National Unity Day Sardar Patel's.

s: National Nutrition Week (1–7 September) is observed by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: National Nutrition Week is observed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

s: Which international agreement does World Ozone Day (16 September) mark?
x: World Ozone Day marks the 1987 Montreal Protocol; its 2026 theme is 'Global Action for a Cooler Planet'.

s: Teachers' Day (5 September) in India marks the birth anniversary of whom?
x: Teachers' Day marks the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, India's 2nd President; observed since 1962.

s: On which date is Ayurveda Day observed from 2025 onwards?
x: From 2025 the Ministry of Ayush fixed Ayurveda Day on 23 September (autumnal equinox).

s: What is the 2026 theme of the International Day of Peace (21 September)?
o: Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day
Global Action for a Cooler Planet
When every voice counts, democracy delivers
x: The 2026 theme of the International Day of Peace is "Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day".

s: What is the 2026 theme of International Literacy Day (8 September)?
o: Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity
Literacy for a world in transition
x: UNESCO's International Literacy Day 2026 theme is "Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity".

s: Hispanic Heritage Month (15 September – 15 October) is observed in which country?
x: Hispanic Heritage Month honours Hispanic and Latino Americans in the US; observed since 1988.

s: What is the 2026 theme of World Patient Safety Day (17 September)?
o: Safe care for every newborn and every child
x: WHO's World Patient Safety Day 2026 theme is 'Safe care for noncommunicable diseases', with the slogan 'Safe care for life!'.

s: What was the theme of the World Space Week, 2022?
o: More than one of the above
x: The United Nations General Assembly declared in 1999 that World Space Week (WSW) will be held each year from October 4-10. "Space and Sustainability" was the theme for the year 2022. The theme for World Space Week 2026 (October 4-10) is “The Rocket Revolution”.

s: What is the theme of World Food Day 2026?
o: End child marriage and invest in girls' rights!
x: The theme of World Food Day 2026 is “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.” The other options are themes associated with the World Congress of Gastroenterology, World Post Day and International Day of the Girl Child.

s: On which date did India join the Universal Postal Union?
x: India joined the UPU on 1 July 1876; the UPU itself was founded on 9 October 1874 through the Treaty of Bern.

s: What is the theme of the International Day of the Girl Child 2026?
o: End child marriage and invest in girls' rights!
x: The 2026 theme of the International Day of the Girl Child is "End child marriage and invest in girls' rights!". The other options are the themes of World Food Day, National Wildlife Week and World Space Week.

s: When is World Space Week, whose 2026 theme is "Rocket Revolution", observed?
x: World Space Week is observed from 4 to 10 October; it was declared by the UN General Assembly in 1999.

s: In which year was the Scinde Dawk, India's first adhesive postage stamp, issued?
x: Scinde Dawk was issued in 1852; stamps were issued nationwide in 1854.

s: In which year was World Food Day first observed?
x: FAO was founded in 1945, the decision on World Food Day came in 1979 and it was first observed in 1981.

s: When was the International Day of the Girl Child, declared by UNGA Resolution 66/170, first observed?
x: It was declared in 2011 by Resolution 66/170 and first observed on 11 October 2012.

s: National Wildlife Week 2026 is observed from 2 to 8 October. It was conceived in 1952 by which organisation?
x: National Wildlife Week was conceived in 1952 by the Indian Board for Wildlife and is observed from 2 to 8 October. The National Board for Wildlife and the Wildlife Institute of India are distinct institutions, while Project Tiger is not the organisation identified with its conception.

s: Where was Beti Bachao Beti Padhao launched on 22 January 2015?
x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly declare World Space Week (4–10 October)?
x: The UNGA declared it in 1999; 1957 (Sputnik 1) and 1967 (Outer Space Treaty) are the events its dates mark.

s: At which UPU Congress was 'UPU Day' renamed World Post Day in 1984?
x: It became UPU Day in 1969 (Tokyo Congress) and World Post Day in 1984 (Hamburg).

s: On which date is National Girl Child Day observed in India?
x: National Girl Child Day is on 24 January; Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015.

s:
Arrange the following October days in calendar order:
1. World Food Day
2. International Day of the Girl Child
3. World Post Day
4. International Day of Rural Women
x: World Post Day is on 9 October, Girl Child Day on 11, Rural Women on 15 and World Food Day on 16 October.

s: The founding of which organisation does World Post Day (9 October) mark?
x: World Post Day marks the founding of the Universal Postal Union on 9 October 1874 by the Treaty of Bern.

s: Which of the following is NOT a UN International Year for 2026?
o: International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists
International Year of the Woman Farmer
International Year of Volunteers for Sustainable Development
x: The three 2026 International Years are Rangelands and Pastoralists, the Woman Farmer, and Volunteers; Glaciers' Preservation was 2025.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Universal Postal Union?
x: The UPU, founded by the Treaty of Bern on 9 October 1874, has its headquarters at Bern.

s: The dates of World Space Week (4–10 October) mark which two events?
o: Sputnik 1 launch and Outer Space Treaty coming into force
Apollo 11 landing and founding of UNOOSA
Sputnik 1 launch and founding of NASA
x: 4 October 1957 is the launch of Sputnik 1 and 10 October 1967 is when the Outer Space Treaty came into force.

s: Gandhi Jayanti is one of how many national holidays of India?
x: Gandhi Jayanti is one of India's three national holidays, with Republic Day and Independence Day.

s: On which date was the Swachh Bharat Mission launched?
x: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2014.

s: When did the Quit India Movement, with the call 'Do or Die', begin?
x: The Quit India Movement began in August 1942 after the Cripps Mission, with the call 'Do or Die'.

s: From what did Gandhi's Kheda movement of 1918 seek relief?
x: Kheda (1918) concerned land-revenue relief; Champaran (1917) concerned indigo cultivators and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) textile workers.

s: Which pair consists of works associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
o: Swaraj in My Ideas and The Discovery of India
Hind Swaraj and The Discovery of India
The Story of My Experiments with Truth and Annihilation of Caste
Hind Swaraj and The Story of My Experiments with Truth
x: Hind Swaraj (1909) and The Story of My Experiments with Truth are both books by Gandhi. Each other option pairs one of them with a book by someone else.

s: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
x: Gandhi returned to India in 1915; he went to England in 1888 and to South Africa in 1893.

s: Which movement or event is correctly matched with its year?
x: The Belgaum Session was in 1924; Non-Cooperation was 1920–22, the Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was in 1931.

s: Where was the only INC session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi held?
x: Gandhi presided over only the Belgaum session (1924) of the INC.

s: As which day does the UN observe Gandhi Jayanti (2 October)?
x: The UNGA in 2007 made 2 October the International Day of Non-Violence; Peace Day is 21 September.

s: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi write Hind Swaraj?
x: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in 1909.

s: Which birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi was marked on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2026?
x: Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869, so 2026 is his 157th birth anniversary.

s: With which cultivators was Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 concerned?
x: Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, for indigo cultivators.

s: On which date did Gandhi begin the Dandi March from Sabarmati?
x: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 and covered about 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi.

s: Where was Mahatma Gandhi born?
x: Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at Porbandar in Kathiawar, Gujarat.

s: Gandhi's Ahmedabad satyagraha of 1918 was a struggle of which group?
x: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 was by textile workers; Champaran (1917) was about indigo and Kheda (1918) about land revenue.

s: Which Round Table Conference did Mahatma Gandhi attend?
x: After the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) Gandhi attended only the 2nd Round Table Conference, as the sole INC representative.

s: With the inscription of the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, how many World Heritage Sites does India have?
x: Sarnath became India's 45th World Heritage Site (Uttar Pradesh's fourth), inscribed under criteria (iii) and (vi).

s: In which year was the UNESCO World Heritage Convention adopted?
x: The Convention dates to 1972; India ratified it in 1977, and the 10 criteria were merged in 2004.

s: The Bagh Cave Paintings, added to UNESCO's Tentative List, comprise how many Buddhist rock-cut caves?
x: Bagh Cave Paintings comprise 9 Buddhist rock-cut caves; Udaigiri has 20 caves.

s: The Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley, included in India's new Tentative List entries, is associated with which combination?
o: Vesara style and Chola and Pallava dynasties
Dravidian style and Gupta and Maurya dynasties
Nagara style and Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata dynasties
Nagara style and Kushana and Satavahana dynasties
x: The Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley represents the Nagara style and is associated with the Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata dynasties. The other options substitute architectural styles or dynasties not associated with this entry.

s: Within which protected area does Ginnorgarh Fort, a new entry on India's Tentative List, lie?
x: Ginnorgarh Fort is in the Ratapani Wildlife Sanctuary and has about 65 stepwells and 4 lakes.

s: In India, which bodies propose sites for UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List?
x: In India the Archaeological Survey of India and INCCU propose Tentative List sites; ICOMOS and IUCN evaluate nominations.

s: Before a site can be nominated for UNESCO World Heritage status, which preliminary requirement must be fulfilled?
o: It must first be placed on the Tentative List
It must first be inscribed on the World Heritage List
It must first receive a transnational serial designation
It must first be declared a natural site
x: A site must be included on the Tentative List before its nomination for UNESCO World Heritage status. Placement on the World Heritage List occurs after the nomination process, not before it.

s: For what are the Bagh Cave Paintings, added to India's Tentative List, known?
x: Bagh's caves carry Buddhist murals; Ahom heritage is Rangpur–Sivasagar, havelis are Shekhawati and Gond heritage is Ginnorgarh.

s: What was the ancient name of Sarnath, the site of the Buddha's first sermon?
x: Sarnath was anciently known as Rishipattan; the first sermon there is known as the Dharmachakra.

s: How many members does the UNESCO World Heritage Committee have?
x: The World Heritage Committee has 21 members.

s: Where was the 48th World Heritage Committee session held, at which Sarnath was inscribed?
x: The 48th session at Busan, South Korea (July 2026) inscribed Sarnath as India's 45th site.

s: In which year did India ratify the UNESCO World Heritage Convention?
x: The Convention was adopted in 1972, but India ratified it in 1977.

s: Which of the following pairs (Tentative List site – feature) is correctly matched?
x: Udaigiri has 20 Gupta-era caves; Bagh has 9 caves, Ginnorgarh is a Gond fort and the Chambal temples are Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata.

s: After the September 2026 additions, India's UNESCO Tentative List has how many sites?
x: Four sites took the list to 73 on 4 September, and five more brought it to 78.

s: With which country does India share the 'Sites of Satyagraha' serial transnational nomination?
x: The 9-component Sites of Satyagraha span India and South Africa (Pietermaritzburg Railway Station, Phoenix Settlement).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List additions and the World Heritage Convention?
o: The Colonial Penal Settlements of the Andaman Islands, including Cellular Jail, were added
Nicobarese Cultural Continuity relates to the Central Nicobar Islands
India ratified the World Heritage Convention in 1972
Shekhawati Painted Haveli Towns are in Rajasthan
x: India ratified the World Heritage Convention in 1977, not 1972.

s: Which of the following is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Uttar Pradesh?
x: Sarnath became UP's 4th World Heritage Site after the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which stupa is a component of the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath inscribed in 2026?
x: The inscribed Sarnath site includes the Chaukhandi Stupa and the archaeological remains.

s: The Rangpur–Sivasagar Historic Ensemble, added to India's Tentative List in 2026, belongs to which dynasty?
x: The ensemble in Assam is Ahom heritage, with the Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and large water tanks.

s: The Udaigiri (Udayagiri) Caves of Madhya Pradesh, with the Varaha panel, were made under which patronage?
x: The 20 Udaigiri caves (4th–5th century) had Gupta patronage; Cave 5 has the Varaha and Cave 13 the Anantasayana Vishnu.

s: Which body evaluates cultural sites nominated for UNESCO World Heritage status?
x: ICOMOS evaluates cultural sites and IUCN evaluates natural sites for the World Heritage Committee.

s: Which of the following is a criterion for granting classical-language status in India?
o: Texts or inscriptions dating back 1,500–2,000 years
A minimum of 500 years of official use
A minimum of 100 years of printed literature
Being spoken by at least one crore people
x: One criterion is texts or inscriptions dating back 1,500–2,000 years; the criteria also include ancient literature and epigraphical evidence.

s: Where is the Centre of Excellence for Bengali as a classical language?
o: Deccan College PG & Research Institute, Pune
x: Bengali's centre is Visva-Bharati; Tezpur is for Assamese, Deccan College for Marathi and Koraput for Pali.

s: Which classical language–year of recognition pair is correctly matched?
x: Sanskrit was recognised in 2005; Tamil in 2004, Telugu and Kannada in 2008, and Malayalam in 2013.

s: How many classical languages does India have after five were added on 3 October 2024?
x: Five languages added in 2024 took the total to 11.

s: Which was the first language to be declared classical in India, in 2004?
x: Tamil was first (2004), Sanskrit in 2005, and Telugu and Kannada in 2008.

s: In which year was Telugu declared a classical language?
x: Telugu and Kannada were declared classical languages in 2008.

s: Where is the Centre of Excellence for Marathi as a classical language?
o: Deccan College PG & Research Institute, Pune
x: The Marathi CoE is at Deccan College PG & Research Institute, Pune.

s: Where is the Centre of Excellence for Pali as a classical language?
x: The Ministry of Education placed the Pali CoE at the Central University of Odisha, Koraput; Prakrit is at the Central University of Gujarat.

s: Where is the Centre of Excellence for Assamese as a classical language?
x: The Assamese Centre of Excellence is at Tezpur University.

s: Where does the Musi river, a tributary of the Krishna, originate?
x: The Musi originates in the Ananthagiri Hills, not the Nilgiri Hills, and is a tributary of the Krishna.

s: Kumik village in Ladakh preserves which canonical Buddhist scriptures?
x: Kumik, known for its Tibetan Buddhist heritage, preserves Kanjur manuscripts, which are canonical Buddhist scriptures.

s: Which place was declared Ladakh's first Heritage Village on 15 September 2026, at the opening of the Zanskar Festival?
x: Kumik in Zanskar, Kargil district, was declared Ladakh's first Heritage Village.

s: In which year was the wooden pagoda-style Hidimba Devi Temple at Manali built?
x: The Hidimba Devi Temple was built in 1553 in wooden pagoda style; Hidimba was Bhima's wife and mother of Ghatotkacha.

s: Which temple near the Ramappa Temple at Palampet, Telangana, was notified as a Monument of National Importance in September 2026?
x: Gollalagudi Temple near the Ramappa Temple got the final notification as a Monument of National Importance; Ramappa itself is the nearby UNESCO-listed temple.

s: Kullu Dussehra, associated with the Kullu region of Himachal Pradesh, is held at which venue?
x: Kullu Dussehra is held at Dhalpur Maidan. Great Himalayan National Park is a UNESCO site, while Dhungri Temple and Shimla Ridge are different locations.

s: What is the capital of Himachal Pradesh?
x: Shimla is the capital; Dharamshala is the winter capital.

s: Under the AMASR Act 1958, up to what distance around a protected monument does the prohibited area extend?
x: The first 100 m is prohibited and the next 200 m regulated.

s: Bhedaghat, known for its Marble Rocks and Dhuandhar Falls, lies on which river?
x: Bhedaghat's Marble Rocks and Dhuandhar Falls are on the Narmada.

s: In which district of Telangana is the Ramappa (Kakatiya Rudreshwara) Temple, a UNESCO site since 2021?
x: The Ramappa Temple is at Palampet in Mulugu district; it was built under the Kakatiyas in the 13th century.

s: After which floods were the Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar reservoirs on the Musi built?
x: Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar were built after the 1908 Musi floods in Hyderabad.

s: Near which place does the Musi river join the Krishna?
x: The Musi rises in the Ananthagiri Hills (Vikarabad) and joins the Krishna near Wadapally in Nalgonda.

s: In which city is the World Congress of Gastroenterology 2026, hosted in India for the first time, being held?
x: WCOG 2026 is scheduled in New Delhi from 1 to 3 October 2026.

s: What is the theme of National Wildlife Week 2026?
o: Bharat's Cultural Connections Across the Globe
x: The theme of National Wildlife Week 2026 is “Connecting Habitats, Thriving Wildlife”. The other options refer to World Space Week, the Brihattar Bharat conference and the World Congress of Gastroenterology.

s: The BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 was inaugurated on 12 October 2026 at which New Delhi institution?
o: Shri Ram Centre for Performing Arts
x: The BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 was inaugurated at the National School of Drama, which also organises Bharat Rang Mahotsav.

s: The Brihattar Bharat International Conference 2026 is organised with the Area Studies Division of which institution?
o: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
x: The conference is organised by Brihattar Bharat and the Area Studies Division of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The 16th National Meeting of State Biodiversity Boards was held in Chandigarh
WWF uses the Giant Panda as its symbol
The National Biodiversity Authority was established in 2003 in Chennai
x: WWF is headquartered in Gland, not Helsinki; its symbol is the Giant Panda.

s: What was the theme of the 27th World Knowledge Forum held in Seoul from September 8–10, 2026?
o: Electric Freight Accelerator for Sustainable Transport
The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order
x: The theme was “The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order.” The forum was held in Seoul and focused on AI and co-intelligence; the other phrases relate to PACT or alter the official theme.

s: The World Circular Economy Forum was launched in 2017 by which Helsinki-based organisation?
x: The World Circular Economy Forum was launched in 2017 by Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, headquartered in Helsinki.

s: The World Circular Economy Forum began during the centenary of which country's independence?
x: The World Circular Economy Forum began during the centenary of Finland's independence.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Green Tribunal (NGT)?
o: Justice Prakash Shrivastava is its Chairperson
Its Chair presented the 5th Swachh Vayu Survekshan Awards
PM Modi inaugurated its conference 'The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics' in September 2026
x: The NGT was established on 18 October 2010, not 8 October; the other statements are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Biodiversity Management Committees maintain People's Biodiversity Registers
The WWF Global Conservation Conference was held in New Delhi
State Biodiversity Boards form the tier between the National Biodiversity Authority and BMCs
The WWF Global Conservation Conference drew representatives from more than 100 countries
x: The WWF Global Conservation Conference was held in Jaipur, not New Delhi.

s: In which year was the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) first held?
x: IFFI was first held in 1952; the National Film Awards date to 1954.

s: IPv6 Internet addresses are how many bits long?
x: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses; IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses.

s: For what does PACT (Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport) pool freight demand?
o: Cruise ships on the East Coast circuit
x: PACT, launched at the 5th e-FAST India Summit, aggregates freight demand for zero-emission vehicles on freight corridors.

s: What was the theme of the 17th Kathakali Festival held at Kalakshetra, Chennai, from September 18 to 20, 2026?
o: Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies
x: The theme of the 17th Kathakali Festival was “Kadha Rasa Sangama.” “Mandodari” was the opening presentation, while “Ramayana” identifies its source tradition; “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies” was the ESTIC 2026 theme.

s: APNIC-62, held in Mumbai from September 4–10, 2026, was hosted by which organisation?
x: NIXI hosted APNIC-62 in Mumbai from September 4–10, 2026. ISPAI was the co-host, while the Maharashtra Government was the supporting partner; APNIC is the Regional Internet Registry for the Asia-Pacific region.

s: What was the theme of the 10th World Circular Economy Forum held at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar, from September 15 to 18, 2026?
o: Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South-South Cooperation
Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies
Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity
x: The theme of the 10th World Circular Economy Forum was "Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity". The other options were the themes of the Kathakali Festival, the Global Dryland Congress and ESTIC 2026.

s: What was the title of the NGT conference inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on September 19, 2026?
o: Transforming Dryland Agriculture with South-South Cooperation
Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity
The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics
x: The NGT conference was titled “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics.” The other options were the themes of the World Circular Economy Forum, the International Film Festival of J&K and the Global Dryland Congress.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the world-first developments reported in September 2026?
o: Chile became the first South American country to eliminate dog-mediated human rabies
Princess Elisabeth Island is being built in the Mediterranean Sea
Belgium is building Princess Elisabeth Island about 45 km offshore for wind power
Chile's last case of dog-mediated human rabies was in 1972
x: Princess Elisabeth Island is being built in the North Sea, not the Mediterranean.

s: Where was the First International Film Festival of J&K (7–10 September 2026) held?
o: National School of Drama, New Delhi
x: The festival was held at SKICC, Srinagar, on Dal Lake, with NFDC.

s: Which organisation coordinated the 2nd Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
x: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research coordinated the 2nd ESTIC 2026, scheduled at Bharat Mandapam from October 27 to 29, 2026. The Department of Defence Production is associated with Aero India, not with coordinating ESTIC.

s: The Brihattar Bharat International Conference 2026 marks the centenary of which organisation?
o: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
x: The conference marks the centenary of the Greater India Society, founded in Calcutta in 1926. Brihattar Bharat and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts are associated with the conference, but the centenary being marked is that of the Greater India Society.

s: The Global Dryland Congress 2026 in New Delhi was organised by which two institutions?
o: NFDC and the J&K Department of Information and Public Relations
x: The Global Dryland Congress 2026 was organised by ICAR and ICRISAT in New Delhi. NBA and WWF, CSIR and ITPO, and NFDC and the J&K Department of Information and Public Relations were linked to other events or organisations.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct in the context of the Global Dryland Congress 2026?
o: ICAR is headed by Director General Himanshu Pathak
ICRISAT, established in 1972, is based in Hyderabad
Drylands cover about 45% of land and are home to more than 2 billion people
x: Himanshu Pathak is Director General of ICRISAT; ICAR's Director General is Mangi Lal Jat.

s: In which year was iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) established?
x: iDEX dates to 2018; India's defence corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

s: Who established the Kalakshetra Foundation, Chennai, in 1936?
x: Rukmini Devi Arundale established the Kalakshetra Foundation in 1936.

s: On which date was the National Green Tribunal established?
x: The NGT was established on 18 October 2010.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian institutions:
1. CSIR was established in 1942.
2. The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October 2010.
3. NITI Aayog came into existence on 1 January 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct; NITI Aayog came into existence on 1 January 2015.

x: The world’s first Copper–Chlorine thermochemical hydrogen plant was established at IGCAR, Kalpakkam, using heat from the FBTR. BARC developed the process and, along with IGCAR, implemented it; therefore, BARC, DAE and FBTR are not the correct locations.

s: Which urban night safari in the world is the Kukrail Night Safari in Lucknow described as?
x: It was described as the fifth urban night safari globally, after Singapore, Thailand, China and Indonesia.

s: Which State abolished its Madrasa Education Board with effect from July 1, 2026?
x: Uttarakhand abolished the board from July 1, 2026, and madrasas are to follow NCERT curricula.

s: Where is India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone, spread over 350 acres, located?
x: The first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, with ₹493 crore from the Centre for Phase 1.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Osmania University's ISO achievement?
o: It became the first university in India with four ISO certifications at once
x: ISO 21001:2018 relates to education; it is ISO 22000:2018 that relates to food safety.

s: India’s first 8-lane tunnel under a tiger reserve is being built under which reserve?
x: The tunnel is under Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve in Rajasthan (formerly associated with Darra Wildlife Sanctuary).

s: Which city became India’s first city under the Easy Connect initiative for international air connections?
x: Varanasi became the first Easy Connect city. Immigration and baggage clearance are completed there before passengers reach Delhi for international connections.

s: Where was India’s first utility-scale Vanadium Redox Flow Battery, with a capacity of 100 MWh, contracted by NTPC REL?
x: The 100 MWh Vanadium Redox Flow Battery is planned at Khavda Solar Park in Kutch. The project was contracted by NTPC REL in July 2026, with completion scheduled for 2027.

s: Which place was identified as India’s first Model Border Village?
x: Chumur in Eastern Ladakh was identified as India’s first Model Border Village. It is being developed under the Vibrant Villages Programme.

s: Near which site was the DPR for India's first offshore airport approved?
x: The offshore airport is planned near Kore Beach, Palghar, as the Mumbai region’s third international airport.

s: Where is India’s first AI hyperscale data centre, developed by Reliance and Meta, located?
x: The data centre is located at Jamnagar. It has a capacity of 168 MW and is Meta’s first Build-to-Suit data centre in India.

s: Which private university established the first IndiaAI Data Lab in collaboration with Intel India?
x: Chandigarh University established the first IndiaAI Data Lab with Intel India. The lab focuses on simulation-based AI projects under the IndiaAI Mission.

s: Which company launched India’s first flex-fuel passenger vehicle that runs on E20 to E100?
x: Maruti Suzuki launched India’s first flex-fuel passenger vehicle, using a sensor to detect the ethanol share.

s: India's first 3D-printed artificial coral reefs were installed off which location?
x: The six 3D-printed artificial coral reef prototypes were installed off Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu, about two nautical miles offshore. Dhanaura is associated with the Wave Sugar ethanol project, while Udaipur is associated with satellite-based jet landing.

s: Where is Wave Sugar's project, India's first private hybrid 2G ethanol project, located?
x: Wave Sugar’s project at Dhanaura produces ethanol from bagasse and crop residue.

s: What is the name of India's first wildlife crime management system developed by the Kerala Forest Department with its technology partners?
x: The system is HAWK, or Hostile Activity Watch Kernel, developed by the Kerala Forest Department with WTI and NTT DATA. GAGAN is used for satellite-based navigation support in aviation, not wildlife crime management.

s: What is the name of India's first indigenous AI video model unveiled by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology?
x: Varya was unveiled by MeitY and built by Avaatar as an indigenous AI video model supporting text-to-video and image-to-video generation. HAWK is the wildlife crime management system, while GAGAN supports aviation navigation.

s: Which satellite-based navigation system enabled India's first satellite-based jet landing by an IndiGo A320 at Udaipur Airport?
x: GAGAN, developed by ISRO and AAI, enabled the first satellite-based jet landing by an IndiGo A320 at Udaipur Airport. LPV is the landing support capability provided by GAGAN, whereas ILS is not required for such GAGAN-supported landings.

s: Where was the foundation laid for India’s first coal-to-ammonium nitrate project?
x: The project is at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda (Odisha) and will make ammonium nitrate from domestic coal via coal gasification and syngas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dam on the Mahanadi – Sihawa Hills
Source of the Mahanadi – near Paradip
x: Ramasi in Bhagalpur is the first Sindoor Village. The Mahanadi rises in the Sihawa Hills, enters the Bay of Bengal near Paradip and has the Hirakud Dam.

s: Which of the following statements about the Army’s first Integrated Battle Groups is incorrect?
o: They are to be formed from 17 Corps, known as Brahmastra.
The first phase includes four IBGs and one Fire Support Group.
They are scheduled to begin from 1 January 2026.
Each IBG is headed by a Major General.
x: The incorrect statement is that they are scheduled to begin from 1 January 2026; the stated date is 1 July 2026. The first IBGs are from 17 Corps, with phase one comprising four IBGs and one Fire Support Group.

s: The first wildlife eco-bridge under the NH-61 expansion in Telangana is being constructed near which place?
x: The first wildlife eco-bridge under the NH-61 expansion in Telangana is being built near Asifabad, linked to the Kawal Tiger Reserve.

s: The Army's first Integrated Battle Groups were raised from 1 July 2026 under which corps?
x: The first IBGs were raised under 17 Corps (Panagarh) – four IBGs and one Fire Support Group in phase 1.

s: Where has India's first 'Sindoor Village' been developed?
x: The Sindoor Village is at Ramasi, Bhagalpur, with Bihar Agricultural University.

s: Where is the world's largest curd plant, whose foundation was laid by Amit Shah in July 2026?
x: The world's largest curd plant of Amul Bengal Dairy is at Sankrail, Howrah.

s: In which country is the first international campus of IIM Bangalore?
x: IIM Bangalore's international campus is at Malang, East Java, Indonesia.

s: Which State passed the Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026?
x: Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026 – a first.

s: Under which BRO project was the world's highest Oxygen Café on a national highway set up in Ladakh?
x: BRO's Project Himank in Ladakh set up the world's highest Oxygen Café on a national highway.

s: The Stree Ride initiative launched in Hyderabad on 6 June 2026 primarily consists of what service?
x: Stree Ride consists of women-driven cabs, autos and bikes in Hyderabad. It was associated with the Women Safety Wing and MOWO and operated on Ola, Uber and Rapido.

s: Navi Mumbai Airport became an authorised port for drug imports from 8 July 2026 by an amendment to Rule 43A of which rules?
o: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
x: The designation was made by amending Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945.

s: Which is the only tiger reserve in Telangana?
x: Kawal Tiger Reserve is the only tiger reserve in Telangana. The other reserves are not identified as Telangana’s sole tiger reserve in the stated fact.

s: As per AISHE 2023–24, what was India's national Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education?
x: National GER rose from 23.7% in 2014–15 to 30% in 2023–24, with a GPI of 1.08.

s: The Cooperative Life Insurance Organization supports which objective of the Ministry of Cooperation?
x: The organisation supports "Sahakar Se Samriddhi", is linked to the proposed National Cooperation Policy 2025 and gives PACS a role.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about interstate water matters?
o: The Tungabhadra High-Power Committee has nine members.
The Sardar Sarovar agreement involves Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra.
The Sardar Sarovar agreement covers cost-sharing and rehabilitation.
The Tungabhadra High-Power Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Cooperation.
x: The Tungabhadra High-Power Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, not the Ministry of Cooperation.

s: Which State became the third State in India to ban Paraquat Dichloride herbicide?
x: Telangana banned Paraquat Dichloride and became the third State to do so. Kerala was the first State in 2011 and Odisha was the second.

s: Telangana signed a cooperation agreement with which German State through the Young India Skills University?
x: The agreement was with Thuringia, whose capital is Erfurt. Mario Voigt is its Minister-President, while A. Revanth Reddy is the Telangana Chief Minister.

s: From which barrage is Rajasthan's share under the Yamuna Water Project to be supplied through underground pipelines?
x: Rajasthan's share is to be supplied through underground pipelines from Hatnikund Barrage under an MoU of the Centre, Haryana and Rajasthan.

s: What is Telangana's Mission K-100, a 100-day plan, for?
x: Mission K-100 is a 100-day plan for Kharif 2026–27 paddy procurement, with a Vehicle Tracking System and implemented with FCI.

s: What is the new name of Jalalabad, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Parshuram?
x: Jalalabad was renamed Parshurampuri, while Bhadarsa was renamed Bharat Nagar.

s: What is the name of the new PMO complex?
x: The new PMO complex is Seva Teerth; the former Rajpath is Kartavya Path.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the nationwide ban on Paraquat is incorrect?
o: Paraquat poisoning can cause fatal outcomes among farmers.
Paraquat is a selective contact herbicide.
Paraquat has already been banned in more than 70 countries.
x: The incorrect statement is that Paraquat is a selective contact herbicide; it is a non-selective contact herbicide. The other statements reflect the reported fatal poisoning risk, absence of a known antidote and its ban in more than 70 countries.

s: Which is the highest technical advisory body under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940?
x: The Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) is the highest technical advisory body under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

s: The nationwide ban on Paraquat, announced by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, falls under which law?
x: The Insecticides Act, 1968 regulates the import, manufacture, sale and use of pesticides; Shivraj Singh Chouhan was associated with the ban.

s: Which organisation is implementing the first phase of Telangana’s Mahila Shakti Super Bazaars?
x: The Mahila Shakti Super Bazaars are being implemented by SERP and run by women’s SHGs. Women Safety Wing and MOWO are associated with the Stree Ride initiative.

s: At the confluence of which rivers is the Gandhi Sarovar project in Hyderabad planned?
x: Gandhi Sarovar is planned at the Musi–Esi confluence; 83.814 acres of defence land were approved under the Equivalent Value Infrastructure policy.

s: For Telangana’s satellite-based crop acreage assessment from Kharif, which institution was entrusted with the work?
o: Osmania University’s Centre for Remote Sensing
x: PJTSAU’s Centre for Digital Agriculture was entrusted with the assessment. It uses remote sensing and GIS and issues reports every 15 days.

s: Who succeeded K. Ramakrishna Rao as Chief Secretary of Telangana?
x: Sanjay Jaju succeeded K. Ramakrishna Rao as Telangana’s Chief Secretary. Jaju was a 1992-batch officer and had served as Secretary, DoNER.

s: Which State was the first in India to ban Paraquat Dichloride, in 2011?
x: Kerala banned Paraquat first (2011), Odisha second and Telangana third.

s: What is the new name of Bhadarsa in Ayodhya district?
x: Bhadarsa became Bharat Nagar; Jalalabad (Shahjahanpur) became Parshurampuri.

s: Where does the Mahanadi river rise?
x: The Mahanadi rises in the Sihawa Hills and enters the Bay of Bengal near Paradip; Hirakud Dam is on it.
